title: Academic background and research
text: Dabit Bista is a PhD candidate in Agricultural, Food, and Resource Economics at Michigan State University. His research uses applied microeconomics, discrete choice experiments, risk preference elicitation, and production economics to study consumer and producer decisions, conservation and natural resources, and sustainable food systems.

title: Working papers
text: Working papers, not peer-reviewed published findings: Measuring Risk Aversion: Evidence from Choice Experiments and Holt-Laury Tasks; The Price of Pasture Rest: Compensation and the Supply of Grazing Management in Conservation Contracts; Technical Efficiency and Producer Risk Preferences in U.S. Cow-Calf Operations. These examine risk measurement, pasture rest compensation, and associations between risk preferences and technical efficiency. Do not claim definitive results.

title: 2026 grazingland publication
text: Merging rigor and relevance in grazingland research: a comprehensive social-ecological monitoring approach. Carbon Balance and Management 21(1), 2026. The public website provides title and citation but not validated detailed results. Do not invent numerical or causal findings.

title: 2024 crop diversification publication
text: Reducing energy and carbon footprint in semi-arid irrigated cropping systems through crop diversification. Heliyon 10(6), e27904, 2024. Public website describes connection between crop diversification, energy use, and carbon-footprint outcomes; precise quantitative findings not yet indexed.

title: 2022 onion publication
text: Effect of Foliar Application of Growth Regulators on Growth and Yield of Onion (Allium cepa). International Journal of Horticultural Science and Technology 9(2), 247–254, 2022. Exact results not provided.

title: 2021 cauliflower publication
text: Ecofriendly Management of Insect Pests of Cauliflower, Brassica oleracea var. botrytis in Kapurkot, Salyan, Nepal. Biopesticides International 17(1), 2021. Exact results not provided.

title: Methods
text: Methods include Ngene efficient discrete choice design, Qualtrics surveys, mixed logit, willingness-to-pay analysis, Holt-Laury risk elicitation, stochastic frontier analysis and technical efficiency.
